_note: Built-in reference map for the Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner revision of the Latin Vulgate). Loaded automatically when the Douay-Rheims edition is detected, so every book name resolves to a canonical OSIS book WITHOUT asking the user to hand-map anything. The Vulgate book naming diverges from later English Bibles in a well-established, unambiguous way — most importantly the Kings/Samuel shift (Douay '1-2 Kings' = Samuel; '3-4 Kings' = Kings) and the Esdras naming (Douay '1 Esdras' = Ezra; '2 Esdras' = Nehemias = Nehemiah). This map is applied PER DOCUMENT (only to files confirmed as Douay-Rheims), so it can never affect a KJV or other edition in the same corpus. Verse numbering is ingested AS PRINTED (Vulgate); the Douay is internally consistent, so this is safe. `key_aliases` is where a Vulgate->Hebrew Psalm cross-reference table would go if you later want the affected Psalms to marry up with Hebrew-numbered editions; leaving it empty keeps the Vulgate numbers as the canonical frame for this edition.

Romans: Epistle of St. Paul to the Romans
Revelation: Apocalypse of St. John the Apostle

key_aliases._note: Empty by design — the Douay is ingested in its own (Vulgate) Psalm numbering. To cross-reference the affected Psalms (Vulgate Ps 9 = Hebrew Ps 9-10; Vulgate is one behind for most of Ps 10-146) with a Hebrew-numbered edition, add entries like {"bible:Ps.<vulgate>.<v>": "bible:Ps.<hebrew>.<v>"} here.
